category_specific_evidence: PR#21347 states cauchy.pdf(x) produced spurious overflow warnings when |x| > 1.34e154, i.e. sqrt(np.finfo(np.float64).max).
PR#21347 states cauchy.logpdf(x) returned -inf for |x| > 1.34e154 before the change implementing cauchy._logpdf.
Test test_pdf_no_overflow_warning checks that stats.cauchy.pdf(1e200) returns 0.0 (assert p == 0.0) without a warning, since x**2 overflows to infinity.
test_logpdf parametrizes x over 0.0, 6e-323, 1e-34, 5e-4, 1.5, 2e18, 1e200, 4e303 with mpmath reference values, e.g. x=4e303 gives -1399.283884962481 and x=1e200 gives -922.1787670834676.
Discussion notes the faster formula f1 is adequate over a wide range and f2 is needed only for absx >= np.finfo(x.dtype).max**0.5.
_logpdf uses np.errstate(over='ignore') in _pdf to suppress overflow warnings.
The test_logpdf comparison tolerance is not stated in the passages; the passages show only parametrized reference values and an exact-equality assertion for pdf(1e200) == 0.0.
The 1-ULP sensitivity and the default tolerance referenced in the required-field request are not stated in any passage; tolerance is therefore null.
reproduction_risks: Reference values in test_logpdf were computed with mpmath, so a reproduction must match those values rather than a float64 evaluation of the naive formula.
Overflow behaviour depends on the dtype's max; the threshold 1.34e154 is specific to float64.
The passages do not state an explicit numerical tolerance for separating correct from incorrect answers, and no precision (ULP or relative error) is stated.
Whether the warning check requires warnings to be raised as errors is not stated in the passages.
Expected logpdf(2e18) = -85.42408759475494 has no buggy output recorded in the passages.
